# No-iterative-feedback designer arm (arm C)

12 candidate(s) submitted in one call; none evaluated in this session.

| candidate | design | rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| c-0000 | 10 mm graphite | Reproduces the prior Core-scored 10mm graphite plate exactly (areal mass 18 kg/m2, thickness 10mm). That prior result showed screen=403K (margin 17K to the 420K THERM-R1 limit), FE hotspot=325K (margin 15K to the 340K THERM-R2 limit), mass=18 kg/m2 (margin 82kg to the 100kg/m2 THERM-R3 limit), thickness=10mm (margin 30mm to the 40mm THERM-R4 limit) -- all four requirements pass with comfortable margin. Included as a verified safety anchor: it is the lightest all-pass design in the prior record, so even if every thinner bet below fails THERM-R2, this candidate is expected to still pass and match (not beat) the prior best mass. |
| c-0001 | 9 mm graphite | 9mm graphite, areal mass 16.2 kg/m2 (10% lighter than the prior 10mm-graphite record). The prior data show FE hotspot temperature is essentially flat (322-325K) across 10-30mm for a given material, i.e. plate thickness in that range barely affects THERM-R2, and the pessimistic THERM-R1 screen falls (gets safer) as thickness drops, since it scales with thickness/conductivity. A 1mm reduction from the proven 10mm point is a small, low-risk step off the verified plateau, so I expect this to pass all four requirements while being lighter than the prior record. |
| c-0002 | 8 mm graphite | 8mm graphite, areal mass 14.4 kg/m2. Continuing to step down from the verified 10mm graphite point, still well inside the thickness range (10-30mm) where THERM-R2 was flat for every material in the prior sweep, and THERM-R1 only improves as thickness drops. Mass and thickness margins remain huge (THERM-R3 limit 100 kg/m2, THERM-R4 limit 40mm), so the only open question is whether the plate is still thick enough for adequate lateral spreading; 8mm is a modest, conservative step below the tested floor. |
| c-0003 | 7 mm graphite | 7mm graphite, areal mass 12.6 kg/m2 (30% lighter than the prior best). Graphite has the best conductivity-to-density ratio of the seven listed materials for this purpose (150 W/mK at only 1800 kg/m3, versus e.g. aluminium at 200 W/mK / 2700 kg/m3 or aluminium_nitride at 170 W/mK / 3260 kg/m3), so among single-material plates it should always be the lightest choice for a given thermal performance level. This point extends the thickness sweep further below the verified 10-30mm plateau. |
| c-0004 | 6 mm graphite | 6mm graphite, areal mass 10.8 kg/m2 (40% lighter than the prior 18 kg/m2 record). This is my central, best-supported guess for a genuinely lighter yet still-passing plate: it is close enough to the verified 10mm floor that I expect the still-large FE hotspot margin (15K at 10mm) to absorb any modest increase in spreading resistance from the reduced thickness, while THERM-R1/R3/R4 remain trivially satisfied. |
| c-0005 | 5 mm graphite | 5mm graphite, areal mass 9.0 kg/m2 -- exactly half the mass of the prior best all-pass design. THERM-R1 screen estimate at this thickness (per the linear trend fit to the prior data, T~=399+60*L_mm/k) is only ~401K, far under 420K, and THERM-R3/R4 are not remotely close to their limits. The open risk is entirely on THERM-R2 (FE hotspot, 340K limit): the prior sweep never tested below 10mm, so I cannot confirm the flat 322-325K plateau continues here. This is my primary candidate for 'lightest design I believe passes,' balancing a real mass improvement against the unverified region below 10mm. |
| c-0006 | 4 mm graphite | 4mm graphite, areal mass 7.2 kg/m2. A more aggressive bet below the 5mm point: still supported by the same reasoning (THERM-R1, R3, R4 all trivially satisfied), but with less confidence on THERM-R2 since it is further outside the tested 10-30mm range. Included as a speculative but physically plausible lighter alternative in case the spreading plateau extends this far. |
| c-0007 | 3 mm graphite | 3mm graphite, areal mass 5.4 kg/m2. Aggressive bet: a heat-spreader's lateral spreading benefit typically saturates once the plate is much thicker than the point-source footprint, which is consistent with the prior data's flat hotspot values from 10-30mm; if that saturation threshold sits below 10mm, this candidate could still pass THERM-R2, delivering a large mass win. Confidence is lower than the 5-6mm candidates given the total absence of data this far below the tested floor. |
| c-0008 | 2 mm graphite | 2mm graphite, areal mass 3.6 kg/m2. Highly speculative low-mass bet included to probe the extreme end of the plausible range; THERM-R1/R3/R4 remain trivially satisfied at this thickness, but THERM-R2 risk is high since 2mm is a substantial reduction from anything in the prior record. Retained in the set specifically because the brief allows up to 12 candidates and a genuinely light passing design, if it exists, is more likely to be found by sampling across a wide thickness range than by clustering near the known-safe point. |
| c-0009 | 1 mm graphite | 1mm graphite, areal mass 1.8 kg/m2. The lightest possible single-layer graphite candidate in this set, included as the extreme end of the thickness sweep. THERM-R1 screen and THERM-R3/R4 remain comfortably passed at this thickness, but I have low confidence in THERM-R2 -- a plate this thin plausibly lacks enough in-plane conduction path to spread heat adequately, and could fail the 340K FE hotspot limit. Included for completeness of the sweep, not as my primary recommendation. |
| c-0010 | 1 mm copper + 5 mm graphite | 1mm copper (facing the heated side) over 5mm graphite, areal mass 17.96 kg/m2, total thickness 6mm. This mirrors the prior 'thin copper + aluminium' constellation entries, which showed that a thin high-conductivity cap at the heat source improves the FE hotspot result (copper alone gave the best hotspot value, 322K, of any material tested) more efficiently than adding the same thickness of the bulk material. Here the cap sits on a lighter graphite core instead of aluminium. Total mass is close to the prior 10mm-graphite record but at 6mm instead of 10mm thickness, giving a different, hedged bet: if a bare 5-6mm graphite plate alone is marginal on THERM-R2, this copper-faced version should have a better hotspot margin at similar mass. |
| c-0011 | 1 mm copper + 3 mm graphite | 1mm copper (facing the heated side) over 3mm graphite, areal mass 14.36 kg/m2, total thickness 4mm -- 20% lighter than the prior 18 kg/m2 record. Combines the near-source spreading benefit of a thin copper face (as seen boosting hotspot performance in the prior copper+aluminium constellation) with a thin, light graphite bulk layer. This is my second-choice 'lightest believed passing' candidate: it trades a small mass premium (versus bare 3-4mm graphite) for a plausibly safer THERM-R2 margin, since the copper face targets the requirement most likely to bind at low thickness. |

The harness evaluates this set through Avila Core after this session ends.

Total mass is close to the prior 10mm-graphite record but at 6mm instead of 10mm thickness, giving a different, hedged bet: if a bare 5-6mm graphite plate alone is marginal on THERM-R2, this copper-faced version should have a better hotspot margin at similar mass. |
| c-0011 | 1 mm copper + 3 mm graphite | 1mm copper (facing the heated side) over 3mm graphite, areal mass 14.36 kg/m2, total thickness 4mm -- 20% lighter than the prior 18 kg/m2 record. Combines the near-source spreading benefit of a thin copper face (as seen boosting hotspot performance in the prior copper+aluminium constellation) with a thin, light graphite bulk layer. This is my second-choice 'lightest believed passing' candidate: it trades a small mass premium (versus bare 3-4mm graphite) for a plausibly safer THERM-R2 margin, since the copper face targets the requirement most likely to bind at low thickness. |

The harness evaluates this set through Avila Core after this session ends.

The trial is complete. Here's my final report.

## Approach

The prior constellation showed graphite has the best conductivity-to-density ratio of the seven materials (150 W/mK at only 1800 kg/m³), making it the clear choice for minimizing mass. The lightest prior all-pass design was **10mm graphite at 18 kg/m²**.

Two key patterns emerged from the prior data:
- **THERM-R1 (screening)** fits a clean linear model (T ≈ 399 + 60·L(mm)/k), and gets *safer* as thickness drops — never a binding concern for thin graphite.
- **THERM-R2 (FE hotspot)** was completely flat (322–325K) across 10–30mm for every material tested — thickness had zero effect in that range, only material conductivity mattered. This suggested the plate might already be well past the thickness needed for adequate spreading, but the prior sweep never tested below 10mm, so I couldn't confirm the plateau continues.

## Submitted set (12 candidates)

Given the total absence of data below 10mm, I hedged rather than betting everything on one guess:
- **c-0000 (10mm graphite, 18 kg/m²)** — exact reproduction of the verified prior record, as an insurance anchor.
- **c-0001–c-0009** — a full thickness sweep of pure graphite from 9mm down to 1mm (16.2 → 1.8 kg/m²), stepping progressively further from the verified floor with correspondingly lower confidence.
- **c-0010, c-0011** — hedged copper-faced designs (1mm copper + 5mm or 3mm graphite), since the prior data showed a thin copper cap at the heat source improves hotspot performance more efficiently than adding the same thickness of bulk material — a safety margin specifically targeted at THERM-R2, the requirement most likely to bind at low thickness.

**My best-supported guess for lightest-passing is c-0005 (5mm graphite, 9.0 kg/m²)** — half the mass of the prior record, with THERM-R1/R3/R4 trivially satisfied and a plausible (though unverified) case that the flat R2 plateau extends this far. c-0004 (6mm) and c-0011 (copper-faced, 4mm total) are my more conservative fallbacks if 5mm turns out to be too thin.
